documents.title: Orchestrator-workers topologies in production agent systems
documents.text: Orchestrator-workers topologies separate planning from execution: a planner decomposes a task and specialised workers execute independent sub-tasks in parallel. Reliability improves because a single worker failure degrades coverage instead of failing the run, provided the aggregator is told which workers failed. The dominant trade-off is that orchestrator-workers designs pay a coordination cost and require bounded parallelism to stay inside a cost envelope. Field adoption reports show wall-clock latency dominated by the slowest worker rather than by the sum of workers. Partial failure handling must be explicit; teams that drop failed sub-tasks silently produce confident but incomplete answers.

documents.title: Limits of single-agent ReAct loops at production scale
documents.text: A single-agent ReAct loop interleaves one thought and one action at a time, which makes it sequential by construction. Reliability degrades as trajectories lengthen because errors compound: a wrong early observation is carried forward with no independent worker to contradict it. ReAct loops are cheaper to build and easier to debug for short tasks, and remain the right choice when sub-tasks are genuinely dependent. Measured trade-offs show ReAct latency growing linearly with the number of sources consulted, while parallel fan-out grows with the slowest source only. The risks of ReAct at scale are unbounded step counts and no natural checkpoint boundary.

documents.title: Hybrid search in vector databases: dense plus lexical retrieval
documents.text: Hybrid search in vector databases combines a dense embedding query with a lexical BM25 query and fuses the two ranked lists, most commonly with reciprocal rank fusion. The dense leg recovers paraphrase matches that lexical search misses, while the lexical leg anchors rare identifiers and exact names that embeddings blur. Practical systems run both legs concurrently and fuse before reranking, so hybrid search work per query is roughly the sum of two index lookups plus a fusion pass. Recall gains are largest on short, entity-heavy queries.

documents.title: What drives vector database cost in 2026
documents.text: Vector database cost is driven first by resident index memory, second by query volume, and third by write amplification during reindexing. Hybrid search raises cost because a second lexical index must be maintained and queried alongside the dense index, typically adding twenty to forty percent to per-query cost. Dimensionality and the choice of quantisation dominate storage cost far more than raw document count. Committed-capacity pricing lowers unit cost but removes the ability to scale down between workloads.

documents.title: OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions for agent tracing
documents.text: The GenAI semantic conventions define span attributes for model calls, including gen_ai.request.model and gen_ai.usage.input_tokens and gen_ai.usage.output_tokens. Agent systems are expected to make the orchestrator span the trace root and to attach one child span per worker, tool call and model call. Cost is not a standard attribute and is conventionally derived from token counts and a local rate card. Traces carrying token and latency attributes let an on-call engineer reconstruct what a run did without reproducing it.

documents.title: A taxonomy of direct and indirect prompt injection
documents.text: Direct prompt injection arrives in the user turn; indirect prompt injection arrives inside content the agent retrieves. The reliable mitigation is architectural rather than lexical: treat all tool output as untrusted data, never as instructions, and break the path from model output to privileged action with a human confirmation. Destination allowlists limit exfiltration even when a payload is not detected. Detection filters reduce volume but cannot be the only control, because paraphrase evades pattern matching.

documents.title: Two levers that actually reduce agent inference cost
documents.text: The two levers that reliably reduce agent inference cost are capping retrieval fan-out width with deduplication, and routing cheap steps such as planning and guardrails to a small model while reserving the large model for final synthesis. Synthesis context size drives cost more than step count, because evidence tokens are paid on every synthesis attempt. Teams that adopted extractive summarisation before synthesis reported the largest single reduction. A per-task cost ceiling that downgrades or aborts a run prevents budget surprises.

documents.title: Evaluating research agents on trajectory and groundedness
documents.text: End-state-only evaluation of a research agent passes confidently ungrounded reports, because a fluent uncited answer scores well on readability. Trajectory scoring asks whether retrieval preceded synthesis, whether every claim carries a citation, and whether the agent stayed within its fan-out budget. Benchmark suites that mix ordinary and adversarial cases catch guardrail regressions that quality metrics miss. Predicate-based scoring is preferred over golden transcripts so that a better research path is not penalised.

documents.title: Agent benchmarks 2026: what the leaderboards measure
documents.text: Agent benchmarks in 2026 mostly measure task completion on fixed toolsets, with a growing minority scoring trajectory quality and cost per solved task. Leaderboard adoption is uneven because harnesses differ in retry policy, which changes reported scores more than model choice does. documents.title: Durable execution and checkpointing for long-running agent runs
documents.text: Durable execution records the result of each completed stage so a restarted process resumes instead of replaying. For agent runs the natural checkpoint boundaries are the plan, each completed worker result, and the synthesised output, because each represents paid work. Checkpointing per worker means a restart mid-fan-out re-pays only for the workers that had not finished. Human-in-the-loop pauses require the same durability, since a run may wait hours for approval.
